s1.syndrome_frame: liver mass with possible metastasis in a patient with history of colon cancer
salient_findings: 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
liver tumor with solid and cystic components
portal vein tumor thrombus suggested by CTAP
key_facts: 55-year-old man
history of right hemicolectomy for adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
staged as IIIB (T4N1M0) colon cancer
no thrombophilic disorders
normal preoperative CEA and CA19-9 levels
completed six months of adjuvant chemotherapy
liver lesion detected 13 months after surgery
hepatitis B and C serologies negative
normal tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II
liver tumor with early phase enhancement and delayed phase washout on CTA
absence of right portal vein and perfusion defect on CTAP
no communication with biliary tree on endoscopic retrograde cholangiography
bile cytology negative for malignancy

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of colon cancer and liver lesion with characteristics suggestive of metastasis

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Liver tumor with early phase enhancement and delayed phase washout, although less likely given normal tumor markers

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Liver mass with possible biliary involvement, although bile cytology was negative for malignancy

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Liver lesion with solid and cystic components, although less likely given patient's history of colon cancer

shortlist.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Liver mass with cystic component, although no communication with biliary tree was found

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, and the liver lesion was detected 13 months after surgery, which is a common timeframe for metastasis. The imaging characteristics of the liver tumor, including early phase enhancement and delayed phase washout, are also consistent with metastatic disease.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: Normal tumor markers, including α-fetoprotein, and no evidence of cirrhosis or hepatitis B/C infection make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: No communication with the biliary tree and negative bile cytology make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Hemangioma
rejected.why: The liver tumor has a solid component and shows early phase enhancement and delayed phase washout, which is not typical of hemangioma

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The liver tumor does not communicate with the biliary tree, and bile cytology is negative for malignancy, making this diagnosis unlikely
